newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly backs Los Angeles secession bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly backs Los Angeles secession bill.

text.p: California's state Assembly approved a bill on Thursday that would make it easier for the San Fernando Valley to secede from the city of Los Angeles.
Assembly Bill 62, by Republican Assemblyman Tom McClintock, cleared the Assembly on a 74-1 vote. It now advances to the state Senate for review.

Under the proposed legislation, a majority of the voters in the city of Los Angeles and in the San Fernando Valley must approve of secession. The bill would also eliminate the power of the Los Angeles City Council to veto the break up.
"It's the fundamental right of any community to decide what type of local government they want to have," McClintock said after the Assembly vote.

The bill, which would apply to other communities in Los Angeles that may also pursue secession, received bipartisan support on Thursday in part because the Los Angeles City Council dropped its longstanding opposition to the proposal, state lawmakers said.
Similar bills failed in the legislature in 1994 and 1996.
